anchor.basis: EIA-860M Operating-sheet snapshot adjusted to Dec 31, 2025 (minus in-service Jan-Sep 2026, plus retired actuals 2026). EIA-derived; ISO-NE CELT publishes capacity on an FCM claimed-capability (SCC/CNRC) basis, not nameplate by fuel, so no CELT table is directly comparable — see cross_checks.

cross_checks.iso_ne_described_generating_capacity_mw: ~29,700 (ISO-NE regional overviews, Mar 2025: 'Nearly 30,000 MW of generating capacity' — FCM claimed-capability basis, not nameplate; excludes settlement-only resources counted differently and all behind-the-meter solar)
cross_checks.definitional_gap: EIA nameplate anchor (38,238.1 MW) exceeds the ISO's ~29.7 GW capability figure by ~8.5 GW. Causes: (1) nameplate vs summer claimed capability — wind, solar and oil steam derate heavily in summer SCC; the EIA anchor on a net-summer basis is 35,426.4 MW, still above CELT because (2) EIA counts every >=1 MW unit incl. small IPP/CHP and settlement-only generators that CELT's generator list treats separately; (3) EIA snapshot includes 1,439.7 MW of non-operating (OS/SB/OA) nameplate; (4) CELT counts ~3,600 MW of demand resources and imports as capacity resources, which are not generation and are excluded here; (5) behind-the-meter solar is in neither the EIA anchor nor the CELT generator list — ISO-NE puts total New England solar nameplate at ~9,600 MW at end-2025 vs 3,734.3 MW of grid solar in this anchor (see README caveats).

trailing.basis: Reconstructed Dec-31 snapshots from EIA unit-level data (Operating Year / Retirement Year). Estimated; not an ISO-NE publication.

diagnostics.exclusion_northern_maine_note: Northern Maine (Maritimes control area; EIA BA code NBSO = New Brunswick System Operator; the northern-Maine system is commonly called NMISA) is not part of ISO-NE and is excluded by the BA cut. Largest item: Mars Hill Wind Farm, 42.0 MW.
diagnostics.ba_boundary_isne_ba_outside_ne_states_no: Small solar units physically in New York state but coded BA=ISNE in EIA (largest: Eureka South/North Solar, 5.0 + 3.5 MW). Included: the cut is by balancing authority, not by state.
